author: TEDx Talks
description:
Most women have spent years changing their bodies for the wrong reasons: to impress a partner, to look good at a reunion, to respond to comments online. Amitis argues that this is why health habits collapse when life gets hard — because the goal was never personal. Drawing on her own experience of losing a business, gaining 65 pounds, and being criticized at both ends of her physical journey, she shares a practical framework for building what she calls ‘Crisis-Proof Confidence’, which is where self-love, not approval, becomes what keeps you going when life gets hard.

Amitis Nate is a professional bodybuilder, fitness coach, and founder of Iron Transform Factory and GuiltlessSweet, where she has helped hundreds of people develop a ‘Winner Mindset’ alongside their fitness goals. With over a decade of experience training women, she brings both professional expertise and hard-won personal insight to the intersection of body image, mental resilience, and lasting confidence.

title: How to set foolproof fitness goals | Amitis Nate | TEDxWest Vancouver Women

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Intelligence is getting cheaper by the day... AI can out-think us in seconds. But cheap intelligence comes with a hidden cost: it's quietly replacing our ability to think, question, and grow wise. 
This talk unpacks why intelligence and wisdom are not the same thing, and introduces a framework for staying irreplaceable in a world that's automating thought itself. David Ajibade is a digital strategist, product and project manager, and AI educator. His work sits at the intersection of technology, profit, business growth and human responsibility This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: The high cost of cheap intelligence | David Ajibade | TEDxFUHSO

author: TEDx Talks
description: AI may be the most powerful general-purpose technology ever built, but its costs are intensely local. Drawing on lessons from the fracking boom, this talk explores how we can design AI infrastructure so communities share in the upside -- not just the burden. Daniel Ketyer is an energy and infrastructure investor and strategic advisor. He is the founder of Riverview, a boutique advisory firm helping companies building the future of energy, robotics, and infrastructure. Daniel grew up in southwestern Pennsylvania during the fracking boom, an experience that shaped his focus on who benefits -- and who bears the costs -- of large-scale technological change. He is a Duke University '16 alum and teaches an undergrad seminar on climate tech venture investing each Fall. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: From Fracking to AI: How to Share the Next Boom | Daniel Ketyer | TEDxDuke

description: Did you know you’re a subject-matter expert based on the experiences you’ve lived through? In this uplifting and inspiring talk, Cassidie Carmen Bates, grief researcher and lived expertise advocate, explores how to identify your most aligned passion and effect resonating change by grounding your pursuits in the expertise only you possess. Cassidie Carmen Bates, MPP, is a grief researcher, a certified grief support specialist, and public policy practitioner. Her work explores how bereavement policies are strengthened when informed by the lived expertise of grievers, in combination with subject-matter data. With nearly a decade of public policy experience, she transitioned into grief policy following the sudden passing of her dad, John. At 25, Cassidie served as the sole executor of her dad’s estate, an experience that demonstrated how little infrastructure exists to support grieving workers. title: Grief, Purpose, and the Power of Lived Expertise | Cassidie Carmen Bates | TEDxDuke

Every other industry has evolved—so why does education still look the same?This talk challenges outdated ideas about schooling and explores why meaningful change has been so slow. It invites audiences to rethink what education should prepare students for in a rapidly changing world. Yahya Ali is an aspiring education reformer with a deep interest in chemistry, learning, and the science of how education shapes human potential. From a young age, he has been driven by curiosity—not only about the natural world but also about how people think, learn, and grow. He believes that education should inspire understanding, creativity, and character rather than memorization alone.

Passionate about lifelong learning and meaningful change, Yahya hopes to contribute to building education systems that empower young minds to think independently and solve real-world problems. description: The excess of institutional violence and dehumanization not only silences Black bodies but attempts to strip them of the very capacity to recognize themselves as human and to envision the future. Faced with a State that fabricates the most impossible justifications to validate its brutality, and where collective pain is turned into spectacle, how can affection and the right to tomorrow be sustained? This poetry-manifesto confronts structural racism to show that where the system plans an end in an instant of terror, the word demands humanity. A multifaceted Afro-artist, TAYÁ makes the word a territory of creation, memory, and resistance. An actress, singer, poet, slammer, visual artist, producer, and cultural activist, she has built a trajectory marked by the meeting of art, ancestry, and social transformation. description: Success is often associated with big milestones such as graduation, launching a business, or standing on a stage. In reality, those moments are only the visible result of countless small decisions made long before anyone notices. In this talk, Abdullah Amir explores the power of the silent shift, the gradual process through which everyday habits, consistent actions, and intentional choices shape our identity and future. Through stories from entrepreneurship, content creation, and public speaking, he demonstrates how ordinary decisions can lead to extraordinary opportunities. This talk challenges the audience to stop waiting for the perfect moment and instead focus on the small choices they make every day, because those choices ultimately become the life they live. Abdullah Amir is an entrepreneur, content creator, podcast host, public speaker, and an undergraduate student at BNU Lahore. title: Small Choices, Extraordinary Outcomes | Abdullah Amir | TEDxTLHC

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Fear of failure is often seen as a massive obstacle, but its most destructive form is a silent shift: surrendering to self-doubt, perfectionism, and self-deceit. A single failure can reshape how we view ourselves, leading to the consequence of living life halfway. This talk explores these internal patterns by connecting literature's timeless questions, like Hamlet's dilemma, with the science of neuroscience. Inspired by how migratory birds navigate invisible pathways, it reveals how small, intentional habits can help rewrite our neural pathways, embrace imperfection, and live more deliberately. Mariam Babar is a student of English Literature, a published author featured in The Writer's Santuary (TWS) and Series of Words anthologies, and an Inspiring Women Ambassador (2025-26). Passionate about the transformative power of literature, she is currently researching children's literature and exploring its role in fostering education, creativity, and critical thinking among young adults.

title: Navigating through the fear of failure and its consequences | Marium Babar | TEDxTLHC

description: Every life is shaped not only by major turning points, but by quiet changes that happen so gradually we hardly notice them. Through stories of migration, grief, language, and belonging, Noor Fatima explores how the ordinary moments we accept eventually become the things we carry with us. Her talk reminds us that the habits, delays, and small choices we normalize today quietly shape the people we become tomorrow. Noor Fatima is a senior student at the Academy for Health and Medical Sciences and a dual-enrollment student at Raritan Valley Community College. She is a Columbia Science Honors Program Scholar, published author, poet, clinical research collaborator, Congressional Award Gold Medal recipient, and Congressional Award National Youth Ambassador. Her work spans healthcare, research, literature, and community service, reflecting her commitment to using science, storytelling, and leadership to create meaningful impact. In her talk, Lisa Johnson explores what it truly means to live a life well lived. Drawing on her journey from poverty and bullying to building a multimillion-pound business, she reflects on why wealth, travel and achievement still left her feeling unfulfilled.
Following the death of her best friend, Lisa began a year-long experiment to leave people feeling better than before they met her, through acts of kindness, support and human connection. She discovered that fulfilment is not determined by what we accumulate or achieve, but by the positive difference we make to others. Her talk invites us to create one meaningful moment of kindness each week. Lisa is a Global Business Strategist and Sunday Times Bestselling author. description: Every day, people postpone difficult conversations because they assume someone else will step in. But what happens when everyone is waiting? Through a deeply personal story of anxiety, rejection, and building a nationwide youth movement, Malaika Mohsin demonstrates how choosing responsibility over hesitation can reshape lives, communities, and cultures. This talk is an invitation to stop waiting and start becoming the change we hope someone else will create. Malaika Mohsin is a mental health advocate, author, and Founder of Sandbox Pakistan, among the country’s first youth-led mental health awareness initiatives and the first in Jhang. She leads a network of 100+ volunteers, organizing support groups, workshops, and advocacy campaigns to reduce stigma and promote well-being. A Psychology graduate from Government College University Lahore, she is pursuing an MS in Clinical Psychology. She explores how class pets may teach responsibility, reduce stress, encourage empathy, and influence the learning environment. Hoeun Sereyoutey is a 9-year-old Grade 4 Earth student at CIA FIRST International School. She enjoys painting, playing the piano, basketball, and swimming. She is a friendly and hardworking student who hopes to become a veterinarian because of her love for animals. Taing Norin Oudom explores how education can move beyond grades by giving students opportunities to learn from mistakes and improve their work. He argues that a growth-oriented approach can strengthen confidence, engagement, creativity, and innovation. Taing Norin Oudom is a student at CIA FIRST International School who enjoys gaming, drawing, and creative problem-solving. His favorite subjects are Computer Science and Visual Arts, and he hopes to pursue a future in software and application development while continuing to grow as an artist. Puthylita Heng explores how seemingly insignificant choices can create powerful ripple effects in people’s lives. Through the symbol of coffee, she reflects on hope, resilience, and the importance of continuing to move forward during difficult moments. Puthylita Heng is a 17-year-old Grade 11 student at CIA FIRST International School. She enjoys reading digital comics and books, playing video games, coding, exploring cafés, and spending time with cats. She values growth, curiosity, and stepping outside her comfort zone.
